item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, leaning slightly positive. AMLO appears to have left many ordinary Mexicans with better material life chances than in 2018, especially through higher real wages, lower labor poverty, broader health coverage, and much larger direct transfers. But the gains were uneven and constrained by persistent violence, impunity, and discrimination, so the improvement is not clean or universal.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Poverty and Inequality Platform, Mexico** — World Bank, 2024 — https://pip.worldbank.org/country-profiles/MEX  
  Claim: World Bank data show Mexico’s national poverty rate at 29.6% in 2024, with bottom-40 consumption growth outpacing the average, which is consistent with improved life chances for lower-income households.  
  IDs: `6B.10`

- **Política social e inversión en la infancia** — UNICEF México, current page using 2024 data — https://www.unicef.org/mexico/politica-social-e-inversion-en-la-infancia  
  Claim: UNICEF says poverty is multidimensional and that in 2020-2024 Mexico reduced child poverty while transfers like Benito Juárez scholarships helped cut child poverty by 4 points over four years, though large structural gaps remain.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`

- **Análisis de la situación de la niñez y adolescencia en México 2018-2025** — UNICEF México, 2025 report using 2024 data — https://www.unicef.org/mexico/informes/situacion-derechos-ninez-adolescencia-mexico  
  Claim: UNICEF reports child poverty fell to 38.7% in 2024 and school/vaccination indicators improved, but 14 million children still lived in poverty and Indigenous children remained far behind, limiting the breadth of life-chance gains.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`

- **Salen de la pobreza laboral 3.2 millones de personas en el último año** — Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social, 2024-09-05 — https://www.gob.mx/stps/prensa/salen-de-la-pobreza-laboral-3.2-millones-de-personas-en-el-ultimo-ano?idiom=es  
  Claim: The labor ministry said labor poverty fell to 35.0% in Q2 2024, 3.2 million people exited labor poverty in a year, and real wages and minimum-wage purchasing power rose sharply, directly improving everyday prospects for low-wage workers.  
  IDs: `6B.10`

- **Misión cumplida: se consolidan Pensiones y Programas de Bienestar** — Secretaría de Bienestar, 2024-09-04 — https://www.gob.mx/bienestar/prensa/mision-cumplida-se-consolidan-pensiones-y-programas-de-bienestar  
  Claim: The government said 14.4 million people received direct, intermediary-free social benefits in 2024, with the old-age pension alone reaching 12.2 million people at much higher real value than in 2018, improving baseline security for older adults and vulnerable households.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`

- **IMSS-Bienestar opera en 23 entidades para atender a 53.2 millones de mexicanos que no tienen seguridad social** — IMSS, 2024-04-17 — https://www.imss.gob.mx/prensa/archivo/202404/170  
  Claim: IMSS-Bienestar covered 53.2 million uninsured people with 131,000 workers, 635 hospitals, and 11,913 health centers, which is strong evidence of expanded access to basic health services for people who inherited weak access.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.9`

- **ACUERDO mediante el cual se establecen las Reglas de Operación del Programa IMSS-Bienestar para el ejercicio fiscal 2024** — Diario Oficial de la Federación / IMSS, 2024 — https://sidof.segob.gob.mx/notas/docFuente/5713366  
  Claim: The 2024 rules define IMSS-Bienestar as a rights-based, professionally administered system with community participation and complaint channels, suggesting an institution that could outlast AMLO’s personal rule.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.9`

- **La Escuela es Nuestra alcanza cobertura del 99 por ciento en planteles de educación básica** — Presidencia de México, 2024-06-26 — https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-escuela-es-nuestra-alcanza-cobertura-del-99-por-ciento-en-planteles-de-educacion-basica/  
  Claim: The school program reached 99% of basic-education schools and handed funds directly to parent committees, which lowers gatekeeping and plausibly improves equal opportunity for children in poorer schools.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.9`

- **Incremento de los salarios mínimos entre 2018 y 2024 es responsable de la mitad de la reducción de la pobreza en el periodo** — Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social, 2025-08-14 — https://www.gob.mx/stps/prensa/incremento-de-los-salarios-minimos-entre-2018-y-2024-es-responsable-de-la-mitad-de-la-reduccion-de-la-pobreza-en-el-periodo?idiom=es-MX  
  Claim: Although published later, it attributes much of the 2018-2024 poverty decline to minimum-wage policy, supporting the view that AMLO’s wage strategy improved ordinary workers’ life chances.  
  IDs: `6B.10`

- **World Report 2024: Mexico** — Human Rights Watch, 2024 — https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico  
  Claim: HRW says AMLO made little progress on extreme criminal violence, abuses against migrants, gender-based violence, attacks on journalists and defenders, torture, disappearances, and extrajudicial killings; it also notes more people lacked health care, which cuts hard against a broad life-chances improvement story.  
  IDs: `6B.10`

- **Mexico: Killings of journalists under state protection show urgent need to strengthen federal mechanism** — Amnesty International / CPJ, 2024-03-06 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/  
  Claim: Journalists under the protection mechanism were still being killed, showing that basic security for a high-risk group remained badly deficient and limiting the real freedom to build a better life.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`

- **Mexico military’s role in migrant massacre comes under sharp scrutiny** — Reuters, 2024-10-16 — https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexico-militarys-role-in-migrant-massacre-comes-under-sharp-scrutiny-3665909  
  Claim: Reuters reported six migrants killed by soldiers, with disputed military accounts, which is direct evidence that vulnerable people remained exposed to lethal harm rather than protected.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`

- **Analysis-Mexico's judicial reform stokes investor fears, though some analysts bullish** — Reuters, 2024-09-17 — https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/analysismexicos-judicial-reform-stokes-investor-fears-though-some-analysts-bullish-3618899  
  Claim: Reuters said the judicial overhaul triggered uncertainty about rule of law and institutions, which matters for life chances because weak legal predictability reduces job, business, and rights security for ordinary people.  
  IDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.9`

**Search gap**
- I found strong data on poverty, wages, health access, and school access, but no single independent 2024 study cleanly isolates AMLO’s causal effect from remittances, pandemic recovery, inflation, and labor-market conditions.
- The positive side is often official self-reporting; the independent side confirms real gains but also shows persistent violence, inequality, and weak protection for several vulnerable groups.
